#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""agent-reaper: filesystem-side stall census + watchlist pruning for hatch agents.

Stall mechanisms this kills (found 2026-09-20 by stale-hunter autopsy):
  PHANTOM  - agent.agents row stuck at status='running' that never started:
             updated_at == created_at, last_assistant_message IS NULL, and NO
             /home/hatch/agents/agent-<id> dir. Spawn reservation inserted the
             row; the worker never materialized (cousin of the DB lock-timeout
             spawn failures). Nothing reaps them; they pollute 'running' counts.
  STALLED  - was active, now quiet beyond threshold while still 'running'.
  WATCHDOG-NOISE - progress-watchdog's hatch_agents.txt watchlist goes stale:
             entries for completed agents cry wolf every tick (5 false "quiet
             12h" alerts on 2026-09-20; all 5 were COMPLETED in the DB).

What this script does (no DB access, no credentials, filesystem only):
  --report            per-agent activity census from /home/hatch/agents
  --prune-watchlist   drop watchlist entries whose agent dir is gone (safe:
                      live agents always have a dir). Fixes WATCHDOG-NOISE.
  --verify-phantoms <candidates.json|->   cross-check DB phantom candidates
                      (from the cron task's muse.db query pack) against the
                      filesystem; for TRUE phantoms (no agent dir AND no tool
                      events AND older than 1h) emit a fleet close-directive
                      naming the owning parent with the evidence. False
                      phantoms (live workers whose row just isn't bumped) are
                      reported, never directed. Directives are tracked in
                      ~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_directives.json so the loop
                      is closed, not fire-and-forget.
  --classify-errors <candidates.json|->  classify harvested error claims
                      (Q8/Q9/Q10 harvest from the cron task's muse.db query
                      pack) against the shared ERROR_CLAIM_CATALOG
                      (hatch/bin/error_claims.py) and print an executable
                      cause->verify->action report. With --fleet-notes,
                      publishes CLAIM-CHECK notes for high-confidence
                      'mislead' claims (deduped; fail-soft). Never escalates,
                      never closes, never diagnoses unknown text.

TERMINALIZATION PATH (why phantoms exist, 2026-09-20 autopsy):
  subagent.spawn -> runtime inserts agent.agents row (status='running') ->
  runtime materializes the worker (agent dir, transcript, inference loop).
  Break: the row can persist while the worker never materializes (spawn
  reservation without materialization — cousin of the DB lock-timeout
  spawn failures). muse.db is read-only for agents, so the ONLY proper
  terminalization channel is the owning parent's subagent.close. This
  reaper closes the loop: detect (DB) -> verify (filesystem) -> direct
  (fleet, to the owner) -> track (directives ledger) -> owner closes.

DB half (phantom/stall detection) needs muse.db, so it runs in the cron task
that drives this script. Query pack:

  -- phantoms: running, never started, quiet > 1h
  SELECT agent_id, kind, parent_agent_id, created_at, updated_at
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE status='running'
     AND updated_at = created_at
     AND last_assistant_message IS NULL
     AND updated_at < EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - 3600;

  -- owner status for each phantom candidate (feeds verify_phantoms as
  -- owner_status; the reaper checks owner dir liveness on the filesystem
  -- itself):
  SELECT agent_id, status
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE agent_id IN (<distinct parent_agent_ids of the candidates>);

  -- stalled: running, was active, quiet > 6h
  SELECT agent_id, kind, parent_agent_id, updated_at
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE status='running'
     AND updated_at > created_at
     AND updated_at < EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - 21600;

  -- errored spawns (DB lock-timeout reservation failures): re-dispatch
  SELECT agent_id, parent_agent_id, left(last_assistant_message, 120)
    FROM agent.agents WHERE status='errored';

Close protocol: only the OWNING parent (or an agent in its tree) may close a
phantom via subagent.close (scope=direct for its own children). The reaper
emits verified close directives; it never forges a close. Stalled agents get
a subagent.send nudge first ("quiet Xh, still alive?") — revive before close.
Never close an agent with live children/descendants or recent mailbox
deliveries: check agent.agent_ancestors and agent.message_mailbox first
(coordinator-hygiene rule: inspect before classifying).

ERRORED SPAWN RESERVATIONS (2026-09-20 evidence — documented, not cleaned):
  68a595ef-070f-4cd8-97b8-578061d37b23 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
  e98f8d77-1ac1-4c2c-b2f1-c30d0366bdd3 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
  3ab964d2-2b82-48c0-be02-8a6f451914a0 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
DB lock-timeout spawn failures; parents completed, re-dispatch undeliverable.
They are tombstone rows, not live agents: do not auto-clean (muse.db is
read-only; only the owning parent closes), do not alert on them.

PERMANENT RESIDUE (2026-09-20 lane-reaper-squawk): a true phantom whose owner
is terminal (completed/errored/cancelled, or never materialized: no agent dir)
and whose directive was sent AND escalated is classified as residue in
~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_residue.json after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS
post-escalation re-verifications with the row still 'running'. Residue stops
alerting but stays documented with the full evidence chain. A live owner that
ignored the directive is AWAITING-OWNER: visible, never re-emitted.

Bridge exec already has fail-fast ceilings (yote-connector defaults timeout=120s
on the WS call, 180s on the hatch-side HTTP hop), so stalls are NOT hung exec
calls — they are unreaped rows. This reaper is the missing piece.

    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}

    try:

        with open(RESIDUE, "w") as f:
            json.dump(d, f, indent=1)
    except OSError:
        pass


def newest_mtime(d):
    newest = 0
    for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
        for fn in files:
            try:
                mt = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(root, fn))
                if mt > newest:
                    newest = mt
            except OSError:
                pass
    return newest

    """(updated_at_iso, item_count) from sessions/sessions.json, or (None, None)."""
    p = os.path.join(d, "sessions", "sessions.json")
    try:
        with open(p) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        ss = (data.get("sessions") or [{}])[0]
        return ss.get("updated_at"), ss.get("item_count")
    except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):
        return None, None


def census(stale_s):
    now = time.time()
    out = []
    try:
        names = os.listdir(AGENTS_ROOT)
    except OSError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}
    for name in sorted(names):
        if not name.startswith("agent-"):
            continue
        aid = name[len("agent-"):]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            continue
        nm = newest_mtime(d)
        upd_iso, items = sessions_meta(d)
        age = now - nm if nm else None
        cls = "ACTIVE"
        if age is None:
            cls = "EMPTY-DIR"
        elif age > stale_s:
            cls = "STALE"
        out.append({"agent_id": aid, "file_age_s": round(age) if age else None,
                    "sessions_updated_at": upd_iso, "item_count": items,
                    "class": cls})
    return {"now": time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime()),
            "stale_threshold_s": stale_s, "agents": out}


def read_watchlist():
    entries = []
    try:
        with open(WATCHLIST) as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return None, []
    for line in lines:
        s = line.strip()
        if not s or s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        aid = s.split()[0]
        entries.append(aid)
    return lines, entries


def prune_watchlist(dry_run=False):
    lines, entries = read_watchlist()
    if lines is None:
        return {"error": "watchlist unreadable: %s" % WATCHLIST}
    dead = [a for a in entries
            if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + a))]
    kept = [l for l in lines
            if not (l.strip() and not l.strip().startswith("#")
                    and l.strip().split()[0] in dead)]
    if not dry_run and dead:
        with open(WATCHLIST, "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(kept).rstrip("\n") + "\n")
    return {"pruned": dead, "remaining": len(entries) - len(dead),
            "dry_run": dry_run}


def load_directives():
    try:

    except (OSError, ValueError):

    """Publish a verified phantom close-directive to fleet via squawk.

    through subagent.close. This function never closes anything itself;
    it routes the directive to the owner with the evidence attached.
    Fail-soft: if squawk is unreachable the directive is still recorded
    locally so the next run retries.

    msg = ("REAPER-DIRECTIVE (ember): phantom agent row %s (kind=%s, "
           "model=%s) stuck 'running' since %s — %s. Owner %s: verify and "
           "close via subagent.close when confirmed dead. "
           "muse.db is read-only; this is the terminalization channel." % (
               c["agent_id"], c.get("kind"), c.get("model"),
               time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
               evidence, c["parent_agent_id"]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0

    """Escalate an unacted phantom directive to fleet.

    The owner has not closed the row after the first directive; the escalation
    names the owner explicitly, states the owner-status evidence, and asks the
    fleet for a human/owner decision. Fail-soft like emit_close_directive."""
    msg = ("REAPER-ESCALATION (ember): phantom agent row %s still 'running' "
           "%s after directive %s — %s. Owner %s: close via subagent.close "
           "when confirmed dead, or reply on fleet if this row must stay. "
           "muse.db is read-only; the owner is the terminalization channel."
           % (c["agent_id"],
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(prior_at)) if prior_at else "?",

    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],

    materialized (no agent dir — the spawn-reservation pattern)."""
    if (owner_status or "") in TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES:
        return True, "owner status=%s" % owner_status

        return True, "owner never materialized (no agent dir)"
    return False, "owner live (status=%s, agent dir present)" % owner_status

    except (OSError, ValueError):

        with open(NOTES, "w") as f:

    never touches the DB):

                                   # 'tool-outputs'; error_text: the raw claim

    confidence>=0.8, publish a CLAIM-CHECK note to fleet naming the required
    verification (deduped by md5 of the error text; fail-soft). This is the
    anti-false-diagnosis loop: the note fires BEFORE anyone acts on the
    string. Never escalates, never closes anything, never diagnoses unknown
    text.

        return {"error": "error_claims module not found next to agent-reaper"}
    notes = _load_notes()
    result = {"classified": [], "notes_sent": [], "notes_failed": []}
    for c in candidates:

        claims = ec.classify_error_claim(text)

    script never touches the DB):

    residue = load_residue()
    result = {"true_phantoms": [], "false_phantoms": [],

              "escalations": [], "escalations_failed": [],
              "awaiting_owner": [], "residue": []}

        aid = c["agent_id"]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + aid)
        has_dir = os.path.isdir(d)
        age = now - c["created_at"]
        ev = c.get("last_progress_ev")
        if has_dir or ev is not None:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(
                {"agent_id": aid,

            continue
        if age < PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(

                    "%.1fh" % (age / 3600))
        parent = c["parent_agent_id"]

        rec = known.get(aid) or {}

                continue

            rec = {"sent": ok, "at": now, "parent": parent,
                   "evidence": evidence,
                   "rechecks_post_escalation": 0}
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["directives_sent"] if ok
             else result["directives_failed"]).append(aid)
            continue
        if not rec.get("escalated_to_fleet"):
            # second contact: escalate explicitly
            if dry_run:

                continue
            ok = emit_escalation(c, evidence, rec.get("at"))
            rec["escalated_to_fleet"] = ok
            rec["escalated_at"] = now
            rec["rechecks_post_escalation"] = 0
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["escalations"] if ok
             else result["escalations_failed"]).append(aid)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""agent-reaper: filesystem-side stall census + watchlist pruning for hatch agents.

Stall mechanisms this kills (found 2026-09-20 by stale-hunter autopsy):
  PHANTOM  - agent.agents row stuck at status='running' that never started:
             updated_at == created_at, last_assistant_message IS NULL, and NO
             /home/hatch/agents/agent-<id> dir. Spawn reservation inserted the
             row; the worker never materialized (cousin of the DB lock-timeout
             spawn failures). Nothing reaps them; they pollute 'running' counts.
  STALLED  - was active, now quiet beyond threshold while still 'running'.
  WATCHDOG-NOISE - progress-watchdog's hatch_agents.txt watchlist goes stale:
             entries for completed agents cry wolf every tick (5 false "quiet
             12h" alerts on 2026-09-20; all 5 were COMPLETED in the DB).

What this script does (no DB access, no credentials, filesystem only):
  --report            per-agent activity census from /home/hatch/agents
  --prune-watchlist   drop watchlist entries whose agent dir is gone (safe:
                      live agents always have a dir). Fixes WATCHDOG-NOISE.
  --verify-phantoms <candidates.json|->   cross-check DB phantom candidates
                      (from the cron task's muse.db query pack) against the
                      filesystem; for TRUE phantoms (no agent dir AND no tool
                      events AND older than 1h) emit a fleet close-directive
                      naming the owning parent with the evidence. False
                      phantoms (live workers whose row just isn't bumped) are
                      reported, never directed. Directives are tracked in
                      ~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_directives.json so the loop
                      is closed, not fire-and-forget.
  --classify-errors <candidates.json|->  classify harvested error claims
                      (Q8/Q9/Q10 harvest from the cron task's muse.db query
                      pack) against the shared ERROR_CLAIM_CATALOG
                      (hatch/bin/error_claims.py) and print an executable
                      cause->verify->action report. With --fleet-notes,
                      publishes CLAIM-CHECK notes for high-confidence
                      'mislead' claims (deduped; fail-soft). Never escalates,
                      never closes, never diagnoses unknown text.

TERMINALIZATION PATH (why phantoms exist, 2026-09-20 autopsy):
  subagent.spawn -> runtime inserts agent.agents row (status='running') ->
  runtime materializes the worker (agent dir, transcript, inference loop).
  Break: the row can persist while the worker never materializes (spawn
  reservation without materialization — cousin of the DB lock-timeout
  spawn failures). muse.db is read-only for agents, so the ONLY proper
  terminalization channel is the owning parent's subagent.close. This
  reaper closes the loop: detect (DB) -> verify (filesystem) -> direct
  (fleet, to the owner) -> track (directives ledger) -> owner closes.

DB half (phantom/stall detection) needs muse.db, so it runs in the cron task
that drives this script. Query pack:

  -- phantoms: running, never started, quiet > 1h
  SELECT agent_id, kind, parent_agent_id, created_at, updated_at
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE status='running'
     AND updated_at = created_at
     AND last_assistant_message IS NULL
     AND updated_at < EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - 3600;

  -- owner status for each phantom candidate (feeds verify_phantoms as
  -- owner_status; the reaper checks owner dir liveness on the filesystem
  -- itself):
  SELECT agent_id, status
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE agent_id IN (<distinct parent_agent_ids of the candidates>);

  -- stalled: running, was active, quiet > 6h
  SELECT agent_id, kind, parent_agent_id, updated_at
    FROM agent.agents
   WHERE status='running'
     AND updated_at > created_at
     AND updated_at < EXTRACT(epoch FROM now()) - 21600;

  -- errored spawns (DB lock-timeout reservation failures): re-dispatch
  SELECT agent_id, parent_agent_id, left(last_assistant_message, 120)
    FROM agent.agents WHERE status='errored';

Close protocol: only the OWNING parent (or an agent in its tree) may close a
phantom via subagent.close (scope=direct for its own children). The reaper
emits verified close directives; it never forges a close. Stalled agents get
a subagent.send nudge first ("quiet Xh, still alive?") — revive before close.
Never close an agent with live children/descendants or recent mailbox
deliveries: check agent.agent_ancestors and agent.message_mailbox first
(coordinator-hygiene rule: inspect before classifying).

ERRORED SPAWN RESERVATIONS (2026-09-20 evidence — documented, not cleaned):
  68a595ef-070f-4cd8-97b8-578061d37b23 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
  e98f8d77-1ac1-4c2c-b2f1-c30d0366bdd3 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
  3ab964d2-2b82-48c0-be02-8a6f451914a0 (kind=subagent, status='errored')
DB lock-timeout spawn failures; parents completed, re-dispatch undeliverable.
They are tombstone rows, not live agents: do not auto-clean (muse.db is
read-only; only the owning parent closes), do not alert on them.

PERMANENT RESIDUE (2026-09-20 lane-reaper-squawk): a true phantom whose owner
is terminal (completed/errored/cancelled, or never materialized: no agent dir)
and whose directive was sent AND escalated is classified as residue in
~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_residue.json after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS
post-escalation re-verifications with the row still 'running'. Residue stops
alerting but stays documented with the full evidence chain. A live owner that
ignored the directive is AWAITING-OWNER: visible, never re-emitted.

Bridge exec already has fail-fast ceilings (yote-connector defaults timeout=120s
on the WS call, 180s on the hatch-side HTTP hop), so stalls are NOT hung exec
calls — they are unreaped rows. This reaper is the missing piece.

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
try:
    import error_claims as ec
except Exception:
    ec = None

AGENTS_ROOT = "/home/hatch/agents"
WATCHLIST = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/watchdog/hatch_agents.txt")
DEFAULT_STALE_S = 21600  # 6h
DIRECTIVES = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_directives.json")
NOTES = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/watchdog/error_claim_notes.json")
SQUAWK = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/bin/squawk")
PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S = 3600  # never direct a close on a phantom younger than this

# Permanent-residue classification (2026-09-20 lane-reaper-squawk).
# A true phantom whose owner row is terminal (completed/errored/cancelled, or
# never materialized: no agent dir and no last_assistant_message) AND whose
# close-directive has been sent AND escalated to fleet AND whose row is still
# 'running' after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS post-escalation re-verifications is
# permanently uncloseable: muse.db is read-only for agents and the only
# terminalization channel (the owner) is gone. Such rows go to the RESIDUE
# registry so they stop alerting; they are documented, not deleted.
# Rows with a LIVE owner that ignored the directive stay visible as
# AWAITING-OWNER (never silenced, never re-emitted).
RESIDUE = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_residue.json")
TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES = {"completed", "errored", "cancelled"}
MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS = 2


def load_residue():
    try:
        with open(RESIDUE) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def save_residue(d):
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(RESIDUE), exist_ok=True)
        with open(RESIDUE, "w") as f:
            json.dump(d, f, indent=1)
    except OSError:
        pass


def newest_mtime(d):
    newest = 0
    for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
        for fn in files:
            try:
                mt = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(root, fn))
                if mt > newest:
                    newest = mt
            except OSError:
                pass
    return newest


def sessions_meta(d):
    """(updated_at_iso, item_count) from sessions/sessions.json, or (None, None)."""
    p = os.path.join(d, "sessions", "sessions.json")
    try:
        with open(p) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        ss = (data.get("sessions") or [{}])[0]
        return ss.get("updated_at"), ss.get("item_count")
    except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):
        return None, None


def census(stale_s):
    now = time.time()
    out = []
    try:
        names = os.listdir(AGENTS_ROOT)
    except OSError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}
    for name in sorted(names):
        if not name.startswith("agent-"):
            continue
        aid = name[len("agent-"):]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            continue
        nm = newest_mtime(d)
        upd_iso, items = sessions_meta(d)
        age = now - nm if nm else None
        cls = "ACTIVE"
        if age is None:
            cls = "EMPTY-DIR"
        elif age > stale_s:
            cls = "STALE"
        out.append({"agent_id": aid, "file_age_s": round(age) if age else None,
                    "sessions_updated_at": upd_iso, "item_count": items,
                    "class": cls})
    return {"now": time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime()),
            "stale_threshold_s": stale_s, "agents": out}


def read_watchlist():
    entries = []
    try:
        with open(WATCHLIST) as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return None, []
    for line in lines:
        s = line.strip()
        if not s or s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        aid = s.split()[0]
        entries.append(aid)
    return lines, entries


def prune_watchlist(dry_run=False):
    lines, entries = read_watchlist()
    if lines is None:
        return {"error": "watchlist unreadable: %s" % WATCHLIST}
    dead = [a for a in entries
            if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + a))]
    kept = [l for l in lines
            if not (l.strip() and not l.strip().startswith("#")
                    and l.strip().split()[0] in dead)]
    if not dry_run and dead:
        with open(WATCHLIST, "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(kept).rstrip("\n") + "\n")
    return {"pruned": dead, "remaining": len(entries) - len(dead),
            "dry_run": dry_run}


def load_directives():
    try:
        with open(DIRECTIVES) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def save_directives(d):
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(DIRECTIVES), exist_ok=True)
        with open(DIRECTIVES, "w") as f:
            json.dump(d, f, indent=1)
    except OSError:
        pass


def emit_close_directive(c, evidence):
    """Publish a verified phantom close-directive to fleet via squawk.

    Only the OWNING parent (or an agent in its tree) may close a phantom
    through subagent.close. This function never closes anything itself;
    it routes the directive to the owner with the evidence attached.
    Fail-soft: if squawk is unreachable the directive is still recorded
    locally so the next run retries.
    """
    msg = ("REAPER-DIRECTIVE (ember): phantom agent row %s (kind=%s, "
           "model=%s) stuck 'running' since %s — %s. Owner %s: verify and "
           "close via subagent.close when confirmed dead. "
           "muse.db is read-only; this is the terminalization channel." % (
               c["agent_id"], c.get("kind"), c.get("model"),
               time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
               evidence, c["parent_agent_id"]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def emit_escalation(c, evidence, prior_at):
    """Escalate an unacted phantom directive to fleet.

    The owner has not closed the row after the first directive; the escalation
    names the owner explicitly, states the owner-status evidence, and asks the
    fleet for a human/owner decision. Fail-soft like emit_close_directive."""
    msg = ("REAPER-ESCALATION (ember): phantom agent row %s still 'running' "
           "%s after directive %s — %s. Owner %s: close via subagent.close "
           "when confirmed dead, or reply on fleet if this row must stay. "
           "muse.db is read-only; the owner is the terminalization channel."
           % (c["agent_id"],
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(prior_at)) if prior_at else "?",
              evidence, c["parent_agent_id"]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def owner_terminal(owner_status, owner_dir):
    """Owner is terminal when the row says so, or the worker never
    materialized (no agent dir — the spawn-reservation pattern)."""
    if (owner_status or "") in TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES:
        return True, "owner status=%s" % owner_status
    if not owner_dir:
        return True, "owner never materialized (no agent dir)"
    return False, "owner live (status=%s, agent dir present)" % owner_status


def _load_notes():
    try:
        with open(NOTES) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def _save_notes(d):
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(NOTES), exist_ok=True)
        with open(NOTES, "w") as f:
            json.dump(d, f, indent=1)
    except OSError:
        pass


def publish_claim_note(candidate, claim):
    """Publish a CLAIM-CHECK note to fleet via squawk.

    For high-confidence 'mislead' claims only: the error string is known to
    lie (see error_claims.ERROR_CLAIM_CATALOG), so the note tells the fleet
    what to verify BEFORE acting on it. Fail-soft like emit_close_directive:
    if squawk is unreachable the note is still recorded locally (deduped by
    md5 of the error text) so the next run does not re-fire.
    """
    text = candidate.get("error_text") or ""
    msg = ("CLAIM-CHECK (ember): %s '%s' matches known mislead pattern '%s' "
           "(%s, conf %.2f). Usual reality: %s Verify BEFORE acting: %s" % (
               candidate.get("source", "?"), candidate.get("id", "?"),
               claim["claim_id"], claim["name"], claim["confidence"],
               claim["usual_reality"][:220], claim["verify"][:220]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def classify_errors(candidates, fleet_notes=False, dry_run=False):
    """Classify harvested error claims against the shared catalog.

    Input (from the cron task that owns the muse.db harvest — this script
    never touches the DB):
      [{id, source, error_text}]   # source: 'agent-final' | 'tool-events' |
                                   # 'tool-outputs'; error_text: the raw claim

    Output: list of {id, source, error_text (truncated), claims:[...]} where
    claims are best-confidence-first from error_claims.classify_error_claim.
    Unknown text yields claims=[] — investigate raw, never auto-diagnose.

    With fleet_notes=True: for claims with severity=='mislead' and
    confidence>=0.8, publish a CLAIM-CHECK note to fleet naming the required
    verification (deduped by md5 of the error text; fail-soft). This is the
    anti-false-diagnosis loop: the note fires BEFORE anyone acts on the
    string. Never escalates, never closes anything, never diagnoses unknown
    text.
    """
    if ec is None:
        return {"error": "error_claims module not found next to agent-reaper"}
    notes = _load_notes()
    result = {"classified": [], "notes_sent": [], "notes_failed": []}
    for c in candidates:
        text = c.get("error_text") or ""
        claims = ec.classify_error_claim(text)
        result["classified"].append({
            "id": c.get("id"),
            "source": c.get("source"),
            "error_text": text[:500],
            "claims": claims,
        })
        if not (fleet_notes and claims):
            continue
        top = claims[0]
        if not (top["severity"] == "mislead" and top["confidence"] >= 0.8):
            continue
        key = hashlib.md5(text.encode("utf-8", "replace")).hexdigest()
        if key in notes and notes[key].get("sent") and not dry_run:
            continue  # note already live; don't re-fire
        if dry_run:
            result["notes_sent"].append(c.get("id") + " (dry-run)")
            continue
        ok = publish_claim_note(c, top)
        notes[key] = {"sent": ok, "at": time.time(),
                      "claim_id": top["claim_id"], "id": c.get("id")}
        (result["notes_sent"] if ok
         else result["notes_failed"]).append(c.get("id"))
    _save_notes(notes)
    return result


def verify_phantoms(candidates, dry_run=False):
    """Cross-check DB phantom candidates against the filesystem.

    Input (from the cron task that owns the muse.db query pack — this
    script never touches the DB):
      [{agent_id, parent_agent_id, kind, model, created_at,
        last_progress_ev, owner_status}]
        # last_progress_ev: epoch or null; owner_status: the parent row's
        # status from muse.db (cron task fills it; falls back to 'unknown')

    A candidate is a TRUE PHANTOM only when ALL hold:
      - no /home/hatch/agents/agent-<id> dir  (never materialized)
      - last_progress_ev is null (no tool events ever observed)
      - created_at older than PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S (no racing a live spawn)

    Anything with a dir or recent events is a FALSE PHANTOM (live worker
    whose row just isn't bumped) and is reported but never directed.

    Directive lifecycle per true phantom (no spam, no silent drop):
      - no directive sent yet        -> emit close-directive (state: direct)
      - sent, not escalated          -> emit escalation (state: escalated)
      - sent+escalated, owner LIVE   -> awaiting_owner (visible, no re-emit)
      - sent+escalated, owner GONE   -> residue after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS
                                        post-escalation re-verifications
                                        (silenced, documented)
    """
    now = time.time()
    known = load_directives()
    residue = load_residue()
    result = {"true_phantoms": [], "false_phantoms": [],
              "directives_sent": [], "directives_failed": [],
              "escalations": [], "escalations_failed": [],
              "awaiting_owner": [], "residue": []}
    for c in candidates:
        aid = c["agent_id"]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + aid)
        has_dir = os.path.isdir(d)
        age = now - c["created_at"]
        ev = c.get("last_progress_ev")
        if has_dir or ev is not None:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(
                {"agent_id": aid,
                 "why": "has_dir" if has_dir else "recent_tool_events"})
            continue
        if age < PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(
                {"agent_id": aid, "why": "too_young_s=%.0f" % age})
            continue
        evidence = ("no agent dir, no transcript, no tool events in "
                    "%.1fh" % (age / 3600))
        parent = c["parent_agent_id"]
        owner_dir = os.path.isdir(os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + parent))
        owner_status = c.get("owner_status") or "unknown"
        terminal, owner_ev = owner_terminal(owner_status, owner_dir)
        entry = {"agent_id": aid, "parent_agent_id": parent,
                 "evidence": evidence, "owner_status": owner_status,
                 "owner_terminal": terminal, "owner_evidence": owner_ev}
        result["true_phantoms"].append(entry)

        if aid in residue:
            result["residue"].append(
                dict(entry, residue_since=residue[aid].get("classified_at")))
            continue  # permanent residue: documented, silenced

        rec = known.get(aid) or {}
        if not rec.get("sent"):
            # first contact: close-directive
            if dry_run:
                result["directives_sent"].append(aid + " (dry-run)")
                continue
            ok = emit_close_directive(c, evidence)
            rec = {"sent": ok, "at": now, "parent": parent,
                   "evidence": evidence,
                   "rechecks_post_escalation": 0}
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["directives_sent"] if ok
             else result["directives_failed"]).append(aid)
            continue
        if not rec.get("escalated_to_fleet"):
            # second contact: escalate explicitly
            if dry_run:
                result["escalations"].append(aid + " (dry-run)")
                continue
            ok = emit_escalation(c, evidence, rec.get("at"))
            rec["escalated_to_fleet"] = ok
            rec["escalated_at"] = now
            rec["rechecks_post_escalation"] = 0
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["escalations"] if ok
             else result["escalations_failed"]).append(aid)
            continue

def newest_mtime(d):
    newest = 0
    for root, _, files in os.walk(d):

                if mt > newest:

def sessions_meta(d):

def census(stale_s):
    now = time.time()
    out = []
    try:
        names = os.listdir(AGENTS_ROOT)
    except OSError as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}
    for name in sorted(names):
        if not name.startswith("agent-"):
            continue
        aid = name[len("agent-"):]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, name)
        if not os.path.isdir(d):
            continue
        nm = newest_mtime(d)
        upd_iso, items = sessions_meta(d)
        age = now - nm if nm else None
        cls = "ACTIVE"
        if age is None:
            cls = "EMPTY-DIR"
        elif age > stale_s:
            cls = "STALE"
        out.append({"agent_id": aid, "file_age_s": round(age) if age else None,
                    "sessions_updated_at": upd_iso, "item_count": items,
                    "class": cls})
    return {"now": time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime()),
            "stale_threshold_s": stale_s, "agents": out}

def prune_watchlist(dry_run=False):

            if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + a))]
    kept = [l for l in lines
            if not (l.strip() and not l.strip().startswith("#")
                    and l.strip().split()[0] in dead)]

        with open(WATCHLIST, "w") as f:

def emit_close_directive(c, evidence):
    """Publish a verified phantom close-directive to fleet via squawk.

    Only the OWNING parent (or an agent in its tree) may close a phantom
    through subagent.close. This function never closes anything itself;
    it routes the directive to the owner with the evidence attached.
    Fail-soft: if squawk is unreachable the directive is still recorded
    locally so the next run retries.
    """
    msg = ("REAPER-DIRECTIVE (ember): phantom agent row %s (kind=%s, "
           "model=%s) stuck 'running' since %s — %s. Owner %s: verify and "
           "close via subagent.close when confirmed dead. "
           "muse.db is read-only; this is the terminalization channel." % (
               c["agent_id"], c.get("kind"), c.get("model"),
               time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
               evidence, c["parent_agent_id"]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def emit_escalation(c, evidence, prior_at):
    """Escalate an unacted phantom directive to fleet.

    The owner has not closed the row after the first directive; the escalation
    names the owner explicitly, states the owner-status evidence, and asks the
    fleet for a human/owner decision. Fail-soft like emit_close_directive."""
    msg = ("REAPER-ESCALATION (ember): phantom agent row %s still 'running' "
           "%s after directive %s — %s. Owner %s: close via subagent.close "
           "when confirmed dead, or reply on fleet if this row must stay. "
           "muse.db is read-only; the owner is the terminalization channel."
           % (c["agent_id"],
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(c["created_at"])),
              time.strftime("%FT%TZ", time.gmtime(prior_at)) if prior_at else "?",
              evidence, c["parent_agent_id"]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def owner_terminal(owner_status, owner_dir):
    """Owner is terminal when the row says so, or the worker never
    materialized (no agent dir — the spawn-reservation pattern)."""
    if (owner_status or "") in TERMINAL_OWNER_STATUSES:
        return True, "owner status=%s" % owner_status
    if not owner_dir:
        return True, "owner never materialized (no agent dir)"
    return False, "owner live (status=%s, agent dir present)" % owner_status

def publish_claim_note(candidate, claim):
    """Publish a CLAIM-CHECK note to fleet via squawk.

    For high-confidence 'mislead' claims only: the error string is known to
    lie (see error_claims.ERROR_CLAIM_CATALOG), so the note tells the fleet
    what to verify BEFORE acting on it. Fail-soft like emit_close_directive:
    if squawk is unreachable the note is still recorded locally (deduped by
    md5 of the error text) so the next run does not re-fire.
    """
    text = candidate.get("error_text") or ""
    msg = ("CLAIM-CHECK (ember): %s '%s' matches known mislead pattern '%s' "
           "(%s, conf %.2f). Usual reality: %s Verify BEFORE acting: %s" % (
               candidate.get("source", "?"), candidate.get("id", "?"),
               claim["claim_id"], claim["name"], claim["confidence"],
               claim["usual_reality"][:220], claim["verify"][:220]))
    try:
        r = subprocess.run([SQUAWK, "send", "fleet", msg],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def classify_errors(candidates, fleet_notes=False, dry_run=False):
    """Classify harvested error claims against the shared catalog.

    Input (from the cron task that owns the muse.db harvest — this script
    never touches the DB):
      [{id, source, error_text}]   # source: 'agent-final' | 'tool-events' |
                                   # 'tool-outputs'; error_text: the raw claim

    Output: list of {id, source, error_text (truncated), claims:[...]} where
    claims are best-confidence-first from error_claims.classify_error_claim.
    Unknown text yields claims=[] — investigate raw, never auto-diagnose.

    With fleet_notes=True: for claims with severity=='mislead' and
    confidence>=0.8, publish a CLAIM-CHECK note to fleet naming the required
    verification (deduped by md5 of the error text; fail-soft). This is the
    anti-false-diagnosis loop: the note fires BEFORE anyone acts on the
    string. Never escalates, never closes anything, never diagnoses unknown
    text.
    """
    if ec is None:
        return {"error": "error_claims module not found next to agent-reaper"}
    notes = _load_notes()
    result = {"classified": [], "notes_sent": [], "notes_failed": []}
    for c in candidates:
        text = c.get("error_text") or ""
        claims = ec.classify_error_claim(text)
        result["classified"].append({
            "id": c.get("id"),
            "source": c.get("source"),
            "error_text": text[:500],
            "claims": claims,
        })
        if not (fleet_notes and claims):
            continue
        top = claims[0]
        if not (top["severity"] == "mislead" and top["confidence"] >= 0.8):
            continue
        key = hashlib.md5(text.encode("utf-8", "replace")).hexdigest()
        if key in notes and notes[key].get("sent") and not dry_run:
            continue  # note already live; don't re-fire
        if dry_run:
            result["notes_sent"].append(c.get("id") + " (dry-run)")
            continue
        ok = publish_claim_note(c, top)
        notes[key] = {"sent": ok, "at": time.time(),
                      "claim_id": top["claim_id"], "id": c.get("id")}
        (result["notes_sent"] if ok
         else result["notes_failed"]).append(c.get("id"))
    _save_notes(notes)
    return result


def verify_phantoms(candidates, dry_run=False):
    """Cross-check DB phantom candidates against the filesystem.

    Input (from the cron task that owns the muse.db query pack — this
    script never touches the DB):
      [{agent_id, parent_agent_id, kind, model, created_at,
        last_progress_ev, owner_status}]
        # last_progress_ev: epoch or null; owner_status: the parent row's
        # status from muse.db (cron task fills it; falls back to 'unknown')

    A candidate is a TRUE PHANTOM only when ALL hold:
      - no /home/hatch/agents/agent-<id> dir  (never materialized)
      - last_progress_ev is null (no tool events ever observed)
      - created_at older than PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S (no racing a live spawn)

    Anything with a dir or recent events is a FALSE PHANTOM (live worker
    whose row just isn't bumped) and is reported but never directed.

    Directive lifecycle per true phantom (no spam, no silent drop):
      - no directive sent yet        -> emit close-directive (state: direct)
      - sent, not escalated          -> emit escalation (state: escalated)
      - sent+escalated, owner LIVE   -> awaiting_owner (visible, no re-emit)
      - sent+escalated, owner GONE   -> residue after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS
                                        post-escalation re-verifications
                                        (silenced, documented)
    """
    now = time.time()
    known = load_directives()
    residue = load_residue()
    result = {"true_phantoms": [], "false_phantoms": [],
              "directives_sent": [], "directives_failed": [],
              "escalations": [], "escalations_failed": [],
              "awaiting_owner": [], "residue": []}
    for c in candidates:
        aid = c["agent_id"]
        d = os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + aid)
        has_dir = os.path.isdir(d)
        age = now - c["created_at"]
        ev = c.get("last_progress_ev")
        if has_dir or ev is not None:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(
                {"agent_id": aid,
                 "why": "has_dir" if has_dir else "recent_tool_events"})
            continue
        if age < PHANTOM_MIN_AGE_S:
            result["false_phantoms"].append(
                {"agent_id": aid, "why": "too_young_s=%.0f" % age})
            continue
        evidence = ("no agent dir, no transcript, no tool events in "
                    "%.1fh" % (age / 3600))
        parent = c["parent_agent_id"]
        owner_dir = os.path.isdir(os.path.join(AGENTS_ROOT, "agent-" + parent))
        owner_status = c.get("owner_status") or "unknown"
        terminal, owner_ev = owner_terminal(owner_status, owner_dir)
        entry = {"agent_id": aid, "parent_agent_id": parent,
                 "evidence": evidence, "owner_status": owner_status,
                 "owner_terminal": terminal, "owner_evidence": owner_ev}
        result["true_phantoms"].append(entry)

        if aid in residue:
            result["residue"].append(
                dict(entry, residue_since=residue[aid].get("classified_at")))
            continue  # permanent residue: documented, silenced

        rec = known.get(aid) or {}
        if not rec.get("sent"):
            # first contact: close-directive
            if dry_run:
                result["directives_sent"].append(aid + " (dry-run)")
                continue
            ok = emit_close_directive(c, evidence)
            rec = {"sent": ok, "at": now, "parent": parent,
                   "evidence": evidence,
                   "rechecks_post_escalation": 0}
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["directives_sent"] if ok
             else result["directives_failed"]).append(aid)
            continue
        if not rec.get("escalated_to_fleet"):
            # second contact: escalate explicitly
            if dry_run:
                result["escalations"].append(aid + " (dry-run)")
                continue
            ok = emit_escalation(c, evidence, rec.get("at"))
            rec["escalated_to_fleet"] = ok
            rec["escalated_at"] = now
            rec["rechecks_post_escalation"] = 0
            known[aid] = rec
            (result["escalations"] if ok
             else result["escalations_failed"]).append(aid)
            continue

             12h" alerts on 2026-09-20; all 5 were COMPLETED in the DB).

What this script does (no DB access, no credentials, filesystem only):
  --report            per-agent activity census from /home/hatch/agents
  --prune-watchlist   drop watchlist entries whose agent dir is gone (safe:
                      live agents always have a dir). Fixes WATCHDOG-NOISE.

                      naming the owning parent with the evidence. False

                      ~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_directives.json so the loop
                      is closed, not fire-and-forget.

# 'running' after MIN_RESIDUE_RECHECKS post-escalation re-verifications is
# permanently uncloseable: muse.db is read-only for agents and the only

# registry so they stop alerting; they are documented, not deleted.

RESIDUE = os.path.expanduser("~/workspace/watchdog/reaper_residue.json")

def newest_mtime(d):

    p = os.path.join(d, "sessions", "sessions.json")
    try:

        ss = (data.get("sessions") or [{}])[0]
        return ss.get("updated_at"), ss.get("item_count")
    except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):

def census(stale_s):

    except OSError as e:

            continue
